title: Underground System
statement:
An underground railway wants to know how long the trips between its stations take. Riders tap their card when they enter a station and again when they leave one. Write an `UndergroundSystem` class with three operations:

- `checkIn id station time`: the rider with card `id` enters at `station` at time `time`.
- `checkOut id station time`: the rider with card `id` leaves at `station` at time `time`. That ends a trip from the station they checked in at, and the trip took `time` minus their check-in time.
- `getAverageTime start end` returns the average time of all the finished trips that went from `start` to `end`. A trip from A to B doesn't count as a trip from B to A, and a rider who hasn't checked out yet doesn't count at all. When no trip from `start` to `end` has finished, it returns `-1`.

The first line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. For each `getAverageTime`, print the average on its own line with exactly 2 decimal places, or print `none` when there's no finished trip. Card ids and times are whole numbers from 0 to 10^6, station names are single words, and times never go down. A rider only checks out while checked in, and the same card can make many trips.

Input:

```text
12
checkIn 45 Leyton 3
checkIn 32 Paradise 8
checkIn 27 Leyton 10
checkOut 45 Waterloo 15
checkOut 27 Waterloo 20
checkOut 32 Cambridge 22
getAverageTime Paradise Cambridge
getAverageTime Leyton Waterloo
checkIn 10 Leyton 24
getAverageTime Leyton Waterloo
checkOut 10 Waterloo 38
getAverageTime Leyton Waterloo
```

Expected output:

```text
14.00
11.00
11.00
12.00
```

hints: Read `checkIn` first. It keeps each rider's check-in in a map by card id, so `checkOut` can look up where and when the trip started.
You never need the trips one by one, only each route's total time and number of trips. Key a map by the pair of stations, start then end.
Divide as decimals, not whole numbers, so that 5 minutes over 3 trips gives 1.67 and not 1.
